result.summary: This PR changes BlockAssembler's chunk-limit check from >= to > so that a mempool chunk which brings the block exactly to block_max_weight or MAX_BLOCK_SIGOPS_COST is included, matching consensus's <= semantics per BIP 141. It extends the existing chunk-limit unit test to cover the exact-equality case for both weight and sigops. The PR is a draft opened specifically to gather concept feedback before further work.
result.problem: BlockAssembler currently rejects a fee-paying chunk when adding it would bring the block exactly to its weight or sigops limit, even though consensus permits blocks at exactly that limit. This leaves a small amount of block capacity and fee revenue unused, an issue raised as item 1 of #35596.

open_concerns: ajtowns: the potential gain (under $1 per block based on typical bottom-transaction fees) is dwarfed by the risk of an accounting off-by-one producing an invalid block and losing the entire ~$240k subsidy; he treats this as not worth doing and says he is unsubscribing from the thread.
ismaelsadeeq: concept ACK, but questions whether the underlying weight/sigops accounting is proven correct enough to remove the defensive buffer; implicitly conditions his support on that confidence.

categories.rationale: P4 because the category file explicitly says changes whose benefit is a small fraction of a block's fees, weighed against invalidity risk, rank low, and this is exactly that case: ajtowns quantifies the upside as under $1 per block against risking the entire subsidy on an accounting mistake. uncertainties: Whether the underlying weight/sigops accounting that this change depends on for safety has been independently verified, which is the crux of ismaelsadeeq's conditional support.
Whether the author intends to respond to ajtowns's cost-benefit objection or will let the PR stall as a draft indefinitely.
result.card: This draft PR flips two >= comparisons to > in BlockAssembler so that a chunk which fills the block exactly to its weight or sigops limit is included, matching BIP 141's <= consensus semantics, and adds tests for the equality case; it addresses item 1 of issue #35596. The problem it fixes is real but tiny: ajtowns estimates the benefit at under $1 per block in extra fees, and argues this is not worth the risk of an accounting off-by-one producing an invalid block and forfeiting the ~$240k subsidy, a concern the author has not answered in two weeks. ismaelsadeeq gave a concept ACK but conditioned it on confidence in the surrounding weight/sigops accounting, which was not established in the thread. The PR was opened specifically to gather concept feedback before further work, and that concept question is exactly where it is currently stuck. No dependencies block it, and it modestly furthers the broader #35596 underfill cleanup.
